mission.finding: The offline harness makes one future technical stream capture falsifiable before provider quota, credentials or raw retention are used.

flexibility.finding: The target, terminal semantics and cap contract are reusable; provider client, decoder and reconciliation remain replaceable future boundaries.

research_truth.finding: No notification is not an empty interval, and transport loss is UNKNOWN. The classifier never projects a technical capture into market or outcome truth.

owner_operability.finding: The Russian readout exposes the effective caps, stop rules and future owner phrase without endpoint or credential disclosure.

execution_to_cashflow.finding: A14 is a read-only technical harness and makes no execution, inventory, settlement, PnL or NetReturn claim.

monitoring_recovery.finding: The bounded foreground shape stops on transport loss and preserves UNKNOWN; reconciliation and any retry decision remain separately authorised.

reuse_first.fit: The existing safety boundary is reused conceptually and through the injected exchange seam without creating a second generic streaming platform.

now.value: The owner can approve or decline one bounded probe with visible limits and a safe stop rule.
now.activation_trigger: The owner decides that this named pool merits one measured technical capture.

watch.value: Replay may reduce recovery uncertainty only if a valid pilot proves that coverage or recovery is the bottleneck.
watch.activation_trigger: A retained technical observation leaves the named consumer blocked on coverage or recovery truth.
